title.narrative: Transforming Household Resilience Through Inclusive Economic Development in South Sudan

description.narrative: THRIVE’s targeting approach is based on intervention levels across different Output areas. The programme distinguishes between entry points (private sector, government, community groups, cooperatives, individuals) and target beneficiaries (vulnerable pastoral, agro-pastoral, and small-scale fishing households).Output 1 engages private sector partners (e.g., fishing/livestock cooperatives) using market diagnostics to improve access and inclusion for marginalized households, especially women.Outputs 2 & 3 focus on community engagement through groups, cattle camps, schools, and local leaders.Output 4 targets women, youth, and persons with disabilities, helping them connect with markets through a cascade model using champions.Geographical targeting prioritizes vulnerable payams/villages using UN/local data, while ensuring inclusion of IDPs, returnees, refugees, and diverse communities. GESI analysis and beneficiary feedback help refine targeting to prevent exclusion. Some emergency aid recipients may also be referred to the programme.

The THRIVE programme seeks to enhance economic and food security while strengthening resilience to conflict and climate shocks for 120,000 households over four years. It employs market systems development and community empowerment approaches, directly supporting 105,000 households and indirectly benefiting 15,000 more along livestock and river corridors.Key outcomes include higher incomes for small businesses in fishing, livestock, and forestry, improved food security, stronger disaster preparedness, better conflict resolution, and women and youth empowerment through financial inclusion and gender equality.Aligned with the SSHARP Theory of Change, THRIVE envisions inclusive and competitive agricultural markets, economically empowered women and youth, and communities capable of managing climate and conflict shocks. By fostering local ownership, peaceful conflict resolution, and sustainable livelihoods, THRIVE aims to create self-reliant, resilient households with reduced dependency on humanitarian aid in Greater Upper Nile.

The THRIVE programme strengthens resilience in conflict- and climate-affected communities across Greater Upper Nile, targeting eight counties in Upper Nile, Unity, and Jonglei States over four years. Led by GOAL, with Mercy Corps, CAFOD, VSF Swisse, and local partners, it will support 120,000 households through livelihood development, market systems, financial inclusion, women’s empowerment, climate adaptation, and social cohesion. Grounded in global best practices and local expertise, THRIVE integrates market systems and community-led approaches to address systemic challenges in pastoral and agro-pastoral value chains, ensuring sustainable economic development and household resilience through inclusive and locally-driven interventions.

activity-date.narrative: Accountable Grant Agreement with FCDO fully signed on 07 November 2024.

recipient-country.narrative: South Sudan faces a protracted humanitarian crisis, with 75% of the population affected by conflict, climate shocks, economic instability, and weak state services. In 2023, 63% of the population is expected to experience ‘crisis or worse’ food insecurity during the lean season.The FCDO funded project titled South Sudan Humanitarian Assistance and Resilience Programme (SSHARP) integrates humanitarian aid and resilience programming in vulnerable areas, focusing on food security, climate adaptation, and protection services, particularly for women and girls. It aims to reduce dependency and improve coordination between emergency and resilience efforts for sustainable impact.
